newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees large E.Europe oilseeds imports.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees large E.Europe oilseeds imports.

text.p: Weather and flood-induced losses in eastern European oilseeds harvests this year will result in higher imports of oilseeds as well as finished oils and meals, the independent newsletter Oil World said.

It forecast the region's net imports of rapeseed at 325,000 tonnes in July/June 1997/98 versus 208,000 tonnes in the previous season, counting Poland, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania as well as former Czechoslovakia and former Yugoslavia.
Combined domestic rapeseed crops by these countries were pegged at 1.24 million tonnes, down 100,000 from last year.
Lower sunseed crops in Bulgaria, Hungary and Romania would reduce the production total in the region to 2.76 million tonnes from 3.1 million last year, Oil World added.
Net sunseed exports were forecast at 240,000 tonnes in 1997/98 after 370,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
Soybean imports into the region were seen rising but total crushings of seeds and beans were still forecast to fall.
The region would import more ready-made vegetable oils and oilmeals in 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) to satisfy rising domestic demand, mostly soymeal, sun oil, rape oil and palm oil.
Gross oil imports in 1997/98 were put at 560,000 tonnes (524,000) and oilmeal imports at 2.15 million (1.97).
